ea337e3ad2.q: What experience prompted a lineman to shift focus toward improving training programs in the power line industry?
ea337e3ad2.a: Christopher Thomas witnessed his first fatality within six months of starting work in West Texas. The incident, where a coworker named Billy Wayne Jr. was killed when an energized structure was hit, revealed critical gaps in training. Thomas realized that training at the time was mostly PowerPoints and slideshows rather than practical instruction, and there was no structured way to learn advanced skills like rigging or transmission work—everything was tribal knowledge passed on informally.
ea337e3ad2.e: 3 Linemen Have A Very Real Conversation | Christopher Thomas & Clint Vick | 222

84d0d2ef2a.q: How did a lineman transition from field work to training leadership at a major power company?
84d0d2ef2a.a: After topping out as a lineman with Local 126, Thomas moved into training roles, first with NLC's mobile team, then with Quanta, before being recruited by George Coleman, president of Powerline & Wireless, to become Director of Training. Coleman offered him the position with a clear mandate: to change the culture and push forward with positive, modernized training approaches rather than traditional classroom methods.
84d0d2ef2a.e: 3 Linemen Have A Very Real Conversation | Christopher Thomas & Clint Vick | 222

57a1d66af3.q: What are the key differences between union and non-union pay structures in the lineman trade?
57a1d66af3.a: When Thomas first encountered union crews working alongside non-union teams on helicopter jobs, he discovered that union linemen with PAR were making triple what he was earning. This exposure to the union's compensation standards prompted him to join Local 126, where he learned about structured union benefits and pay scales that non-union workers did not receive.

9622879163.q: What measurement system inconsistencies affect daily work in the power line industry?
9622879163.a: The power line industry uses metric measurements from utilities (millimeters, centimeters) for standards, but physical infrastructure like poles, bolts, and arms are measured in feet and inches. Additionally, linemen often measure travel distances in time rather than miles or kilometers—for example, a job site might be described as 'an hour away' rather than a specific mileage, which provides a more practical sense of the workday.
9622879163.e: 3 Linemen Have A Very Real Conversation | Christopher Thomas & Clint Vick | 222

89cf519e21.q: How does the transition from field work to office-based roles affect lineman mental health and identity?
89cf519e21.a: Christopher Thomas explains that moving from fieldwork into supervisory or office roles happens almost without realization—you simply stop being out on the poles one day. Clint Vick adds that this transition is not widely discussed in the industry, but it can be psychologically difficult: losing the camaraderie of crew work, no longer being able to interact with crews the same way, and realizing retrospectively that all your photographs were of work rather than family moments.
89cf519e21.e: 3 Linemen Have A Very Real Conversation | Christopher Thomas & Clint Vick | 222

7903fe7900.q: What role did military service play in Christopher Thomas's path to the lineman trade?
7903fe7900.a: Thomas joined the Marine Corps right out of high school and served approximately 15 years before entering the lineman trade. He was approached by the guy running the NLC campus while on a plane headed to Brazil for volunteer work, who convinced him that linework was a viable career path in California with good earning potential.

b6c9f38783.q: What statistics demonstrate the disproportionate mental health crisis among construction workers compared to the general population?
b6c9f38783.a: In 2023, construction workers died of overdose at over 10 times the rate they died from job site injury. Additionally, male construction workers die by suicide at a rate of 75% higher than men in the general population. Furthermore, only 5% of trades workers have consulted a mental health professional versus 22% of the general population.
b6c9f38783.e: What If Mental Health Was Treated Like Jobsite Safety? | Wykisha Thomas-McKinney, Nate Strickland & Tyler Smith | 221

db11c61ddf.q: How does prolonged time away from family on job sites contribute to mental health deterioration in construction workers?
db11c61ddf.a: Workers spend 12 to 14 hours a day on jobs, often for extended periods in remote locations like man camps or hotels, creating profound isolation. When they return home for short stints, they often feel like strangers in their own homes because their families have established routines without them. Unresolved relationship conflicts accumulate over months because they cannot be addressed through phone or FaceTime, and social media now constantly reminds workers of family moments they are missing, creating additional emotional weight.
db11c61ddf.e: What If Mental Health Was Treated Like Jobsite Safety? | Wykisha Thomas-McKinney, Nate Strickland & Tyler Smith | 221

eaeeaa3548.q: What is the Mates North America program and how does it address suicide prevention in construction?
eaeeaa3548.a: Mates North America is a pilot program launched in February that is built off a model developed in Australia over 20 plus years ago. The program goes to construction sites and builds what is called a network of safety by training volunteers called connectors on how to ask about suicide, provide support, and care for their colleagues. The program also provides Advanced Suicide Intervention Skills Training for those who want to go further, similar to having someone CPR certified on every site but for mental health. The program establishes trust and relationship through toolbox talks, social events, and ongoing site engagement, recognizing that…

4e1fe8814d.q: What role do hobbies, exercise, and comprehensive mental health planning play in preventing mental health crises among construction workers?
4e1fe8814d.a: Mental health should be treated like physical health—it requires a comprehensive plan including physical activity, outdoor hobbies, meaningful social connections, and professional mental health support. Workers benefit from finding outlets outside of work such as exercise, building projects, or making phone calls to family and friends. The research shows that just being present with somebody and showing that you care reduces the risk of suicide, and developing a mental health plan as part of overall health helps prevent reaching the point of needing hospitalization or medication.
4e1fe8814d.e: What If Mental Health Was Treated Like Jobsite Safety? | Wykisha Thomas-McKinney, Nate Strickland & Tyler Smith | 221

743b106b76.q: How does the construction industry culture of suppressing emotions affect mental health outcomes?
743b106b76.a: In line work and construction specifically, feelings are discouraged from being discussed, with the expectation to put your game face on and get work done. Workers bottle up their thoughts during working hours and then suffer alone with those thoughts at night in hotels or man camps. This culture of silence means that depression, anxiety, and suicidal thoughts are not addressed until they reach critical levels, and workers do not seek help-seeking behavior before it becomes a crisis requiring medication or hospitalization.
743b106b76.e: What If Mental Health Was Treated Like Jobsite Safety? | Wykisha Thomas-McKinney, Nate Strickland & Tyler Smith | 221

fbe819448a.q: What are the relationship and social factors that research identifies as central to suicide risk in construction workers?
fbe819448a.a: Research at Mates shows that one of the main factors related to mental health challenges and even suicidal thinking is relationship issues—problems with spouses, family, and children. Having access to people that care about you reduces the risk of suicide, and being part of a network or group where people can help guide you through isolation is essential. Isolation from family combined with unresolved relationship conflicts that cannot be fully addressed due to physical distance creates compounding mental health risk.
